Hi Samira,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the candid walkthrough of CareBridge's ingestion pipeline and the privacy constraints. Quick recap and the asks we captured on our side so we can align the technical follow-up: 

1) Logging scope (what you saw today)
   - Request/response bodies: you indicated sensitive PHI/PII occasionally appears in the request payloads.
   - Headers: a subset contain internal trace IDs and partner tokens that must not be stored in cleartext.
2) Residency & retention
   - US-only residency required for production data.
   - Retention target: you asked for options down to 0–7 days for hosted logs; longer retention acceptable for debug environments.
3) Audit & evidence
   - SOC 2 report and evidence of log redaction controls (how masking/pseudonymization is implemented).

Immediate next steps we proposed on the call:
- I’ll share a short matrix of logging options (attached) with recommended defaults for a pilot.
- Ben to follow up with concrete implementation choices (masking vs hashing, trace id pseudonymization) and pilot plan.
- Samira to share the procurement timeline and point person from Legal/Privacy for the questionnaire.

Proposed technical demo: 30 minutes (tech + ops) — available Tue/Wed next week 10–11am PT. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Attachments: redwood_logging_options.csv (stub) — small matrix with config toggles.

Open questions from our side to help size the pilot:
- Rough QPS / peak requests for the endpoints that will be instrumented?
- Do you have a sample (sanitized) request/response example that reproduces how PII appears today?

Happy to sync and iterate — want to keep the pilot narrow so we can demonstrate the redaction controls without touching your main retention settings.

Best,

Jonas — thanks for the recap. Confirming a few priority items from our side so the pilot addresses the compliance gate: 

- We cannot have request/response bodies retained in cleartext in hosted environments. If you need bodies for debugging, they must be pseudonymized or stored only in an isolated staging environment.
- Trace IDs and any token-like headers must be removed or irreversibly hashed before storage; reversible encryption is not acceptable for production logs.
- For the procurement/legal team: we’ve attached a short vendor security questionnaire — legal will expect SOC 2 Type II and controls that demonstrate log-sanitization.

Availability for the technical demo: Wed 2027-05-19 10:30–11:00am PT (works best).

Hi Samira — appreciate the clarity. Wanted to put concrete technical options on the table so Legal and DevOps can pick the right tradeoffs quickly. Short answers up front, fuller details below.

TL;DR
- Hosted: default retention 30 days for debug logs; configurable down to 0 days (no logs persisted) for request/response bodies. Headers can be suppressed at the ingress layer.
- Pseudonymization: we support irreversible hashing (HMAC-SHA256 with per-customer salt) for trace IDs and other header values. Hash outputs are stored for 7 days by default for troubleshooting; can be set to 0 days.
- Private deployment: if you require no-hosted-storage, our Private (VPC) deployment can be configured to never persist request/response bodies and keep only aggregated metrics.

Details / Options
1) Request/response body handling
   - Option A (Strict): Do not log request/response bodies at all for production endpoints. Only structured metadata and metrics retained.
   - Option B (Hash & sample): Apply deterministic salted HMAC to PII fields and store only hashed values + a 0.1% sampled raw payload in a staging project for debug (sample retained separately). Sampling is opt-in.
2) Header suppression & trace ID policy
   - Header suppression list: you can provide a regex or explicit header names; those are stripped at the edge.
   - Trace ID policy: if you need the ability to correlate requests across services, we can store a pseudonymized trace_id (HMAC) for up to N days. The raw trace id is never persisted.
3) Retention & residency
   - Hosted US regions only for your account.
   - Retention configurable per-environment (prod/staging). By default: prod bodies=0 (if you choose Option A) / traces hashed for 7 days.
4) Evidence & audits
   - SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA; we can provide redaction control artifacts and a short implementation whitepaper.

Pilot proposal (recommended minimal scope)
- Enable header suppression for the three headers you flagged (X-Partner-Token, X-Internal-Trace)
- Enforce Option A for production endpoints (no body logs) and Option B hashed traces for staging with 7-day retention
- Provide a short implementation plan and a Jira ticket for the engineering handoff

What we need from you to scope work:
- Expected peak QPS for the instrumented endpoints (estimate is fine).
- A sanitized sample payload (DevOps mentioned they will provide by Tue).
- Confirmation whether Legal will accept HMAC-based hashing (irreversible) for trace correlation.

I attached a more detailed CSV matrix (same file Jonas referenced) but expanded with config values and estimated engineering effort. Happy to run through it in the demo and lock down the pilot config.

Best,
